comments.author: @ItaliaThroughTime
comments.text: There's a saying in Italy that Venice is an upside-down forest: millions of tree trunks pointing down into the mud instead of up to the sky. The Republic took its forests so seriously that it protected whole woods on the mainland just for its ships, like the beech forest of the Cansiglio, kept for the oars of the Arsenal. Venice wasn't only built on water, it was built on centuries of careful forestry. Beautiful footage, as an Italian I really enjoyed it.
